note.text:
Every point of the perpendicular bisector of [AB] is at the same distance from A and from B: if P is on it, then PA = PB.
The converse is also true: if a point P has PA = PB, then P is on the perpendicular bisector of [AB].
So the perpendicular bisector of [AB] is the set of all the points that are equidistant from A and B (at equal distances).
If PA is not equal to PB, P is not on the perpendicular bisector.
Two points that are each equidistant from A and B are enough to draw the perpendicular bisector: it is the line through them. That is why the construction works: the crossing points of the arcs are at the same distance from A and from B.
A triangle PAB with P on the perpendicular bisector of [AB] is isosceles: PA = PB.

worked_example.problem: P is on the perpendicular bisector of [AB]. PA = {pa} cm and AB = {ab} cm. Find PB and the perimeter of triangle PAB.
steps: P is on the perpendicular bisector of [AB], so P is at the same distance from A and B: PB = PA = {pa} cm.
Perimeter = PA + PB + AB = {pa} + {pa} + {ab} = {two * pa + ab} cm.
worked_example.answer: PB = {pa} cm and the perimeter is {two * pa + ab} cm.

example: QA = {x} cm and QB = {x} cm: Q is on the perpendicular bisector.

cards.idea: Two points that are each equidistant from A and B fix the perpendicular bisector: it is the line through them.
example: CA = CB and DA = DB, so C and D are both on the perpendicular bisector of [AB].
The perpendicular bisector of [AB] is the line (CD).

solution: {P[0]} and {P[1]} are both equidistant from A and B, so both are on the perpendicular bisector.

questions.prompt: P is on the perpendicular bisector of [AB]. PA = {pa} cm and AB = {ab} cm. Find the perimeter of triangle PAB.

misconceptions.explain: PB is a side too, and PB = PA = {pa} cm.

solution: P is on the perpendicular bisector, so PB = PA = {pa} cm.

questions.prompt: P is on the perpendicular bisector of [AB]. The perimeter of triangle PAB is {2 * pa + ab} cm and AB = {ab} cm. Find PA.

misconceptions.explain: That is PA + PB. PA is half of it, because PA = PB.

solution: PA = PB, so PA + PB = {2 * pa + ab} − {ab} = {2 * pa} cm.

solution: A point is on the perpendicular bisector of [AB] exactly when it is at the same distance from A and B.
Only {N[0]} has equal distances, so the answer is {answer}.
